newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices down, NYC sale ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices down, NYC sale ahead.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices opened a touch weaker in virtually non-existent trade ahead of New York City's $808 million tax-exempt deal.
"I feel like the Maytag repairman this morning," a trader said, adding that his desk was "pretty much just sitting here waiting for someone to call us."
Wednesday morning's session continued the pattern of the past three weeks, the trader said. While Street inventory remains light, buyers are not rushing to buy bonds either, he said.

"You have a little toe-tapping on one side, a little on the other side, but not much of a market and not much action at all," the trader said. "If I had to make it up, I would say the market was down 1/8, but there really haven't even been any trades so far."
Despite it's size, the New York City deal is unlikely to exert much supply pressure, and instead should benefit from paper scarcity.
"They are attractive and I think it will take care of itself, " the trader said. "I mean they have a lot of it presold from what I can see."
A second trader said estimates called for a 6.32 percent top yield on the City's offering.
"Maybe they'll bump it, they increased the size by a lot," the trader said. The deal had earlier been said to total $550 million.

Including the City's deal, scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $1.667 billion in 29 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales are expected to total $418 million million in 14 sales.
The largest is a $195 million North Carolina general obligation bond issue at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales are expected to total $1.249 billion in 15 offerings. The City's deal through Goldman Sachs & Co is the largest.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 9/32 at 114-25/32. The March T-bond contract was down 8/32 at 111-5/32. The MOB spread was 117 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 12/32 at 96-5/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
